related_work: Seth Giddings discussed his book Toy Theory, which explores technology through play rather than just practical use. Yaqian Lai introduced how maps have been used in art, both in analogue and digital forms.
conclusion_future_work: This week made me realise that interaction does not always need a specific purpose or outcome. I would like to explore how playful interactions could make my previous ideas more engaging and accessible.
results_discussion: The assignment asked us to design a toy rather than a game. This made me think about the difference between playing freely and following rules to achieve a goal.I started thinking about whether I could extend my previous idea of collecting animal behaviours and natural signs into an interactive toy.For example, users could explore a digital map and interact with different animals or natural elements. Each interaction could reveal a traditional interpretation or an unexpected visual response.Rather than creating a system that gives correct predictions, I could focus on encouraging curiosity and exploration.
title: week 4
introduction: This week, we explored the relationship between toys, technology and map art. I was interested in the idea that technology does not always need to solve a problem. It can also encourage people to play, explore and imagine.
